clue.text: Urge president to provide transport for youngster

parts.note: to urge someone on is to push them
the chair is the person presiding over a meeting

explanation.surface: Pressing a president to lay on a vehicle for a child.
explanation.definitionFit: A folding wheeled seat is how a small child gets carried about, so it is transport for a youngster.

clue.text: Singer uses one piano in place of orchestra

indicators.note: in places the two letters inside the word for the orchestra's place

parts.note: the orchestra pit is where a theatre band plays
I is the Roman numeral one
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A singer using a single piano instead of a full orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer' suggests an opera performer, but it is a songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: This small brown bird is a songbird, a natural singer.

clue.text: He's got the hump, sailing over the sand

definitions.text: He's got the hump, sailing over the sand

parts.words: He's got the hump, sailing over the sand
parts.note: a humped beast that crosses the desert as a vessel crosses the sea, while 'got the hump' sounds like being sulky

explanation.definitionFit: The camel carries travellers across the desert as a vessel crosses the sea, hence its nickname.

clue.text: Possibly drag lake officer has obsession about

indicators.note: about means the officer and obsession go round the letter for lake

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer
to have a thing about something is to be obsessed by it

explanation.surface: An officer with a fixation about a lake being dragged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drag' looks like a verb about dredging a lake; it is women's dress worn by a man. 'Possibly' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Drag is a style of dress, an example of what people wear.

clue.text: Be indecisive, having abandoned western state

indicators.note: having abandoned means the letter for western is dropped

parts.note: to waver is to be indecisive

explanation.surface: Wavering over leaving a western American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Western state' looks like a US state; 'state' is a verb meaning declare.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to declare or assert firmly.

clue.text: New chorister quiet in church office

indicators.note: new means the letters of chorister are made into something fresh

parts.note: P is piano, quiet in music

explanation.surface: A new chorister keeps quiet in a church job.
explanation.definitionFit: The post held by a parish clergyman is a church office.

clue.text: Panorama series originally framed by Sackville-West

indicators.note: something framed by another piece sits within it, so one set of letters goes inside the other

parts.note: Vita Sackville-West was an English writer and garden designer

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word series

explanation.surface: A television documentary series first shown with Sackville-West as its presenter.
explanation.walkthrough: Panorama looks like the BBC current-affairs programme, but it is just a wide view.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweeping view over a landscape is a panorama, the same idea as a long prospect.

clue.text: Sound sailor in shameful situation

indicators.note: in puts the sailor inside the shameful word

parts.note: vile means shameful
AB is an able seaman

explanation.surface: A healthy sailor caught in a disgraceful situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Situation' just rounds out the surface: the sailor is situated in VILE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound plan is one that can work, which is feasible.

clue.text: Conform, following current movement

definitions.meaning: to go along with what everyone else does
literally a swimmer moving along with the flow of water

explanation.definitionFit: Going along with the prevailing trend is to conform, and a swimmer going with the flow follows the current.

clue.text: Lincoln bishop caught in some corrupt behaviour

parts.note: Abe Lincoln, the US president
RR is Right Reverend, a bishop's title

indicators.note: in places the cricket letter inside the word for some

parts.note: any means some
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A bishop of Lincoln caught in some corrupt behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lincoln bishop' looks like a cathedral city's prelate; Lincoln is Abraham.
explanation.definitionFit: Straying from right conduct is deviance, a departure from the norm.

clue.text: Source of trouble dignified church woman carries about

indicators.note: the first word carries the next piece inside it, as a container

parts.note: dignified bearing is poised
on means about, as in a talk on a subject
Alice is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A stately churchwoman carrying something around with her.
explanation.definitionFit: An honour or post that brings hidden harm is idiomatically a tainted cup, so a source of trouble.

clue.text: Left back presented with extremely heavy cup

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for left in reverse

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

indicators.note: extremely means take the two extreme letters of heavy

explanation.surface: A footballer playing at left back receives a very heavy cup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left back' reads as the football position; it is PORT reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup awarded to a winner is a prize, the commonest kind of trophy.

clue.text: See about flag, say, draped round fan

indicators.note: one piece draped round another encloses it

parts.note: a flag is an iris, an example of a flower

indicators.note: about tells us to turn the word for see backwards

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see

explanation.surface: Inspecting a flag that has been draped around a supporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' is the iris plant, not a banner; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan is an admirer or supporter of a team or star, which is what an adherent is.

clue.text: It purifies us from a share in concupiscence

parts.note: concupiscence is strong sexual desire, lust
a ration is a share

explanation.surface: Something that cleanses us of our part in sinful desire.
explanation.definitionFit: A ritual washing is a cleansing ceremony that purifies the worshipper.

clue.text: Former partner can effuse about current put out

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
a tin is a can

indicators.note: about puts the gushing word round the letter for current

parts.note: to effuse is to pour out, gush
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: An ex can gush about the latest news being released.
explanation.definitionFit: To put out a fire or light is to quench it.

clue.text: Refreshments girl's offered round flat as I left

indicators.note: offered round means put round the flat word
left means the letter I departs

parts.note: Elsie's, a girl's name in possessive
taken as written
even means level, flat

explanation.surface: A girl's snacks being passed round the flat as someone leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the girl's possessive S counts as a letter. 'Left' removes the I, leaving ELSES, and 'offered round' wraps that round the word for flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevenses is the British mid-morning snack, a light refreshment around eleven o'clock.

clue.text: Shock we've got mad about

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for mad is read backwards

parts.note: nuts is slang for mad

explanation.surface: Someone admits we have gone crazy about something.
explanation.definitionFit: To shock someone is to daze or stagger them.

clue.text: Censure companion upholding imitation article

indicators.note: in a down clue the companion holds up the rest, so it comes last

parts.note: a repro is a reproduction, an imitation
A is the indefinite article
CH is Companion of Honour

explanation.surface: Criticising a companion for supporting a fake item.
explanation.definitionFit: To reproach someone is to rebuke or censure them.

clue.text: Reportedly exploit wool producers

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: to exploit something is to use it

explanation.surface: Rumours of wool producers being exploited.
explanation.definitionFit: Female sheep grow the fleece that is shorn for wool.

clue.text: How some protest, knowing about ballistic missile!

indicators.note: about places the word for knowing around the missile

parts.note: a knowing look is a sly one
Trident is Britain's submarine-launched ballistic missile

explanation.surface: Protesters shouting knowingly about a nuclear missile.
explanation.definitionFit: Protesters often shout harshly and loudly, which is the adverb's sense.

clue.text: Asian lines up to be received by Welshwoman

indicators.note: received by means taken inside the woman's name

parts.note: Sian is a Welsh woman's name

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read upwards, reversed

parts.note: RY is short for railway lines

explanation.surface: An Asian queues up to be welcomed by a woman from Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Syria is in western Asia, so a native is an Asian.

clue.text: Typical person highly involved in backing VIP

indicators.note: involved in means put inside the other piece
backing says read the word for a VIP backwards

parts.note: a celebrity is a name
highly means very

explanation.surface: Someone ordinary who is deeply involved in supporting a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: The archetypal ordinary person is the man in the street, the average individual.

clue.text: Minister meddles with final part of act

parts.note: one who pries meddles in others' business

indicators.note: final part of means the last letter of act

explanation.surface: A government minister interferes with the last scene of a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' suggests a politician; here it is a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister of religion is a clergyman, like a parish priest.

clue.text: Meeting held in Coventry Street

indicators.note: held in means the letters sit inside Coventry

explanation.surface: A rendezvous arranged in a Coventry street.
explanation.walkthrough: The hidden part gives only TRY; ST comes from Street.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryst is a lovers' secret rendezvous, a meeting.

clue.text: Gelatinous substance obtained from a fish

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A jelly-like substance taken from a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Agar is a jelly made from seaweed, used in labs and cooking.

clue.text: Particular seriousness relative to chemists?

parts.note: specific means particular
gravity means seriousness

explanation.surface: A specially serious relative of some pharmacists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relative' looks like a family member; it is the adjective, as in relative density.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemists measure a substance's density relative to water, which is the ratio this term names.

clue.text: Smooth and silky, as armchairs may be.

definitions.meaning: a glossy smooth finish, like the fabric of that name
armchairs are things people have sat inside

explanation.definitionFit: The fabric is glossy and smooth, and a chair that has been used has been sat in.

clue.text: Direction we accepted in old PM's time

indicators.note: accepted in means taken inside the following pieces

parts.note: Lord North was British prime minister 1770 to 1782
taken as written

explanation.surface: A direction we followed in an earlier prime minister's era.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord North was the prime minister when Britain lost the American colonies.
explanation.definitionFit: A compass point between two cardinal points is a direction.
